newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian women journalists decry political murders.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian women journalists decry political murders.

text.p: Nigerian women journalists ended a conference in the eastern city of Owerri on Saturday decrying recent murders of three women politicians.

Meeting under the aegis of the Nigerian Association of Women Journalists (NAWOJ) they said in a communique that the killings were meant to scare women from participating in military ruler General Sani Abacha's transition to civil rule programme.
"NAWOJ urges women to remain undaunted and to reinforce themselves for active participation in the transition programme," the group said.

The latest of the unsolved murders of top women in Nigeria took place two weeks ago when Suliat Adedeji, a member of the advisory committee of the National Centre Party of Nigeria, was shot dead in her home in Ibadan, southwestern Nigeria.

In June the senior wife of detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola was shot while in traffic in Lagos and later died in hospital. Soon after an 80-year-old industrialist, Madam Bisoye Tejuosho, was hacked to death in her home.
"The recent murders of Mrs Kudirat Abiola, Madam Tejuosho and Alhaja Adedeji are dastardly acts that should be condemned by every Nigerian," NAWOJ said.
Nigeria has been in political turmoil since 1993 when a presidential poll, which Abiola is presumed to have won, was annulled by a previous military government.

Abacha, who seized power in the chaos that erupted after the annulment is implementing a plan he says will lead to election of a president in 1998 but before then there are several other elections scheduled to fill municipal and state level posts.
